waypoints.name: Paradise
waypoints.directions: From SR 7 at Elbe, take SR 706 east through Ashford to the Nisqually Entrance, then follow the park road past Longmire to Paradise at about 5,400 ft, roughly 19 miles from the entrance. Overnight parking is allowed only in designated areas, and from November the road above Longmire is gated every night. A park entrance pass is required, plus a climbing permit for glacier travel or above 10,000 ft.

waypoints.name: Columbia Crest
waypoints.directions: Take the Skyline Trail about a mile to Glacier Vista, drop west off the moraine and cross the Nisqually Glacier roped, then climb the boulder gully on the far side and Wapowety Cleaver to camp near 9,000 to 9,500 ft. Cross the Wilson Glacier to the wide couloir with the hourglass, climb it, bear left onto the upper Nisqually above 11,000 ft to the saddle between Point Success and the crater rim, then go up onto the rim to Columbia Crest.

waypoints.name: White River Campground
waypoints.directions: From Enumclaw, drive SR 410 east to the White River Entrance of the park and turn west onto the Sunrise Road. After about 5 miles, cross the White River and turn left onto the White River Campground road, following it to its end. Park in the day-hiking and climbing lot at about 4,400 ft; the Glacier Basin Trail starts in the campground's D loop. The road is open in summer only, and a park entrance pass is required.

waypoints.name: Killen Creek Trailhead
waypoints.directions: Reached on Forest Roads 23, 21 and 2329 from the Randle or Trout Lake side. FR-2329 holds snow well into early summer, so check the road before committing — parties blocked short of the trailhead have had to walk or bushwhack an extra mile or more of road and forest to reach it.

waypoints.name: High Camp Trail Junction
waypoints.directions: Follow Killen Creek Trail #113 up through subalpine forest and meadow for about three miles to the Pacific Crest Trail, and cross straight over onto the High Camp Trail. Killen Creek, crossed low on the trail, is the last dependable running water; everything above is melted snow. The tread thins out above treeline and is easy to lose in the dark or a whiteout, so note landmarks on the way up or carry a track.

waypoints.name: High Camp
waypoints.directions: Another mile on the High Camp Trail ends it at the edge of the Adams Glacier's lateral moraine. Sheltered bivy sites sit slightly higher, in a shallow snow gully just left of the moraine, and more camping is scattered across the benches above that.

waypoints.name: Adams Glacier Base
waypoints.directions: A patchy path runs past the upper camping area and up moraine and snow to the glacier toe, where parties rope up. Judge the timing generously — the volcano's scale flattens distance out and this leg routinely runs two hours. The point of the very early start is to be through the icefall before the sun starts working on it.

waypoints.name: Mount Adams Summit
waypoints.directions: The usual line takes the right-hand side of the glacier for roughly the first two-thirds, threading ice steps and serac lanes, then cuts back left high up onto the unbroken snow of the summit plateau. Which side of the upper icefall goes changes from year to year, and the left-hand option has been found far steeper than the grade suggests — sustained 55 to 65 degrees rather than moderate — so look at it in daylight from below before committing. The crossing beneath the ice cliffs is the stretch to move through fastest, on thin bridges and with backtracking common. Above the icefall the angle eases and two or three false summits stand between you and the true one, so keep navigating rather than trusting the first high point.

waypoints.name: Heliotrope Ridge Trailhead
waypoints.directions: The trailhead sits at roughly 3,400 to 3,700 ft on Glacier Creek Road 39. The road washed out in December 2025 and reopened to vehicles in August 2026 after repairs; it has washed out before, so check its status before committing.

waypoints.name: Heliotrope Ridge Camp
waypoints.directions: Trail 677 climbs through old-growth forest and flower-filled avalanche chutes, with a couple of unbridged creek crossings that are awkward early season or after rain. At about 2.25 miles the maintained trail forks; the left branch goes to the Coleman Glacier overlook, so take the right climbers' path that drops toward the moraine. Past the former Kulshan Cabin site near 4,800 to 5,000 ft, the last reliable running water, the path climbs steeply up the crest of the Hogsback lateral moraine to the usual camps between about 6,500 and 7,200 ft, roughly 3 to 3.5 miles and 3,000 ft above the car. Above camp there is no water except what you melt.

waypoints.name: Coleman Headwall Base
waypoints.directions: Rope up for glacier travel and cross the broken lower Coleman, generally trending up toward 8,000 ft to meet the North Ridge tracks before dropping back down and cutting under the Roman Nose to reach the base near 8,500 ft. This crossing is a real route-finding crux that changes year to year, with big crevasses to weave around, questionable snow bridges, and sometimes a committing, barely-reversible jump or a short vertical step to get established. Leave camp in the dark (starts between 11 p.m. and 4:30 a.m. are typical) so you are past the exposed crossing and the lower face before the sun brings rock and ice down off the headwall and the Black Buttes.

waypoints.name: Mount Baker Summit
waypoints.directions: Roughly a dozen pitches of sustained 45 to 50 degree neve and ice lead up the face: hard, dirty ice on leftward-trending traverses low down with rockfall exposure from a choss band above, then short steeper steps and an 800 ft band of brittle, plated 60 to 80 degree ice that takes screws well despite looking suspect. A bergschrund near 10,000 ft is the other crux and its lip often forces a short, occasionally overhanging step, sometimes belayed or lowered across off a screw or picket. Above it the angle relents to moderate snow and then an easy slope onto the summit plateau; 8 to 12 hours camp-to-summit is typical.

waypoints.name: Artist Point Trailhead (Chain Lakes/Ptarmigan Ridge Trail)
waypoints.note: Park Glacier Headwall approaches from Artist Point on the opposite side via Ptarmigan Ridge, not from Glacier Creek Rd/Heliotrope Ridge.
waypoints.directions: From I-5 Exit 255 in Bellingham, follow the Mount Baker Highway (WA-542) east through Glacier and past the Heather Meadows ski area to the road end at Artist Point, about 58 miles. The final stretch is usually snow-free only from about mid-July into early fall. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

waypoints.name: Grant Peak (Mount Baker summit)
waypoints.directions: Follow the Chain Lakes Trail about a mile to the Ptarmigan Ridge junction, then the Ptarmigan Ridge Trail west along the crest past Coleman Pinnacle and Camp Kiser to the Portals, where most parties camp. Drop onto the Rainbow Glacier, cross onto the Park Glacier, and climb the headwall beneath the Cockscomb, crossing the bergschrund near 9,500 ft, to the summit plateau and Grant Peak.
